seal_dust.title: Sharp, dry dust that is also cold
seal_dust.why: Regolith grinds seals, joints and bearings; cold stiffens them.
seal_dust.gap: Earth wind rounds some grains; no electrostatic cling from sunlight.
seal_dust.moon: Diviner: dust at the poles sits under 126 K on average, far colder than any Earth dust test.

low_sun.title: Low sun and black shadows
low_sun.why: Cameras, lidar and eyes face glare beside total darkness.
low_sun.gap: Earth air scatters light into shadows; they never go fully black.
low_sun.moon: LOLA: 11% of ground within 5 degrees of the pole is in permanent shadow, so robots drive in and out of total darkness.

deep_cold.title: Deep cold
deep_cold.why: Shadowed crater floors freeze machines and hold the ice.
deep_cold.gap: Best ice-free ground covers about 26% of the gap; the rest needs a chamber.
deep_cold.moon: Diviner: coldest crater floors never pass 27 K (-246 C) even at noon in summer. 99% of ground south of 80S averages colder than Earth's record low air (184 K).

lunar_night.title: Two weeks of night
lunar_night.why: Landers must ride out 14 days of dark and cold on stored power.
lunar_night.gap: Earth air and wind move heat; the Moon only radiates it away.
lunar_night.moon: Diviner: half the ground south of 80S averages under 126 K (-148 C) across the year.

thermal_swing.title: Big daily temperature swings
thermal_swing.why: Repeated hot-cold cycles crack joints, solder and seals over years.
thermal_swing.gap: MODIS: Earth's ground swings reach about 31 C from day to night; Mars about 80 C; the Moon far more.
thermal_swing.moon: Diviner: summer highs south of 80S run from 187 K to 286 K, while yearly averages sit near 126 K.

thin_air.title: Thin, dry air and strong UV
thin_air.why: Low pressure and UV drive equipment cooling, materials ageing and crew health.
thin_air.gap: Earth's highest ground keeps about half its air; Mars has under 1%.
thin_air.mars: MOLA terrain: half of Mars has under 624 Pa of air; even the deepest basin has 1258 Pa. Earth's highest bare ground still has about 81 times the median Mars pressure.

pad_rock.title: Rocky, flat ground to build landing pads
pad_rock.why: Engine blast sprays loose regolith; pads must be built from local rock on flat ground.
pad_rock.gap: Rocket plume in vacuum spreads farther than in air; gravity 1/6.
pad_rock.moon: LOLA 40 m slopes: the sunniest ground (where a base and pad would go) has a median slope of 5 degrees, and 84% is under 10. Test sites should be that flat.

dry_permafrost.title: Ice locked in dry frozen ground
dry_permafrost.why: Ice cemented into soil is the water and fuel source, and fights drills.
dry_permafrost.gap: Earth ground ice is warmer and younger than lunar cold-trap ice.
dry_permafrost.moon: Diviner: ice is stable within 1 m of the surface on 38% of ground south of 80S. Where it is buried, the median dry cover is 8 cm (90% under 49 cm). That is the depth a drill test must match.

featureless.title: Flat, featureless ground
featureless.why: Robots lose track of distance travelled when nothing in view changes.
featureless.gap: Earth light and haze still give visual cues the Moon lacks. Ice sheets are even flatter but are ice, not ground.
featureless.moon: LOLA 40 m slopes: median 9 degrees near the pole; 20% of ground is steeper than 15 degrees, so long featureless runs are rarer there than on the maria.

no_compass.title: No usable compass
no_compass.why: Neither world has a global magnetic field to steer by.
no_compass.gap: Field near the magnetic pole is weak, not absent, and it moves each year.

power_ridge.title: Ridges with sun that never sets
power_ridge.why: Solar farms on crater rims that see the sun most of the time.
power_ridge.gap: Earth's midnight sun lasts weeks to months; cloud still interrupts it.
power_ridge.moon: LOLA: the sunniest spot within 5 degrees of the south pole is lit 88% of the time, but only 0.8 km2 is lit more than 70%. Earth's midnight sun gives 50% at most over a year.

sun_ice_edge.title: Sunlit ridge next to frozen ground
sun_ice_edge.why: The best base sites sit on the edge: power on the rim, ice in the crater below.
sun_ice_edge.gap: Our Earth grid is 18 km; the lunar commute is under 1 km, so pick the exact spot locally.
sun_ice_edge.moon: LOLA: from ground lit over 70% of the time, permanent shadow is a median 350 m away (90% within 0.9 km). The engine now requires sun and frozen ground in the same 18 km cell.

mars_hyperarid.title: Cold, hyperarid, sterile ground
mars_hyperarid.why: Mars soil is bone dry with oxidizing salts that hurt crops and life detection.
mars_hyperarid.gap: Earth deserts still have trace life and liquid fog; no global perchlorate map was used.
mars_hyperarid.mars: Odyssey gamma-ray map: even the dry low latitudes hold a median 4% water by weight, locked in salts and minerals (1.6 to 7.4%). The Earth test is getting water out of bone-dry, salty soil.

radiation.title: Highest natural cosmic-ray exposure
radiation.why: Space radiation flips bits and wears electronics; Earth's thinnest shielding is high ground near the magnetic poles.
radiation.gap: Earth's air and field still block most of it; a lunar surface dose is far higher.

radiative_cold.title: Heat lost straight to the sky
radiative_cold.why: With no air, hardware cools only by radiating to space; radiators and night heaters are sized for that.
radiative_cold.gap: Earth air still carries heat by convection, unlike the Moon.

dust_devils.title: Dry, fine dust lifted by heat: static and dust devils
dust_devils.why: Mars dust devils and charged dust coat solar panels and optics; robots must clean or ride it out.
dust_devils.gap: Earth dust devils are smaller and wetter than Mars's.
dust_devils.mars: TES albedo: 25% of Mars is bright, dust-covered ground that devils and storms can lift.

soft_sand.title: Soft sand that traps wheels
soft_sand.why: Spirit ended its drive stuck in soft sand; rovers need to detect and escape it.
soft_sand.gap: Earth gravity presses wheels harder into the sand than Mars does.
soft_sand.mars: TES thermal inertia: 70% of Mars between 60S and 60N is sand or crusted soil, and 22% is loose dust. Spirit died in soft soil under a crust.

dust_storm.title: Windy, dusty plains
dust_storm.why: Dust storms cut solar power for weeks and sandblast hardware.
dust_storm.gap: Martian storms can wrap the whole planet; Earth's are regional.
dust_storm.mars: TES albedo: 25% of the planet is dust-mantled, the source for regional and global storms.

dust_mantle.title: Deep loose dust, not sand
dust_mantle.why: Mars data shows a fifth of the planet is fine dust a rover sinks into, not dune sand. Wheels, drills and suits behave differently in each.
dust_mantle.gap: Earth dust is rarely more than a few cm deep outside dry lakebeds; Mars mantles can be metres thick.
dust_mantle.mars: TES thermal inertia: 22% of Mars between 60S and 60N reads under 100, which means loose, fine dust. This test exists because the Mars data asked for it.

lava_tubes.title: Lava tubes and caves in young basalt
lava_tubes.why: Lava tubes could shelter crews from radiation, impacts and temperature swings. Robots must learn to find, enter and map them.
lava_tubes.gap: Earth tubes are younger, wetter and smaller; lunar tubes may be far wider in low gravity.
lava_tubes.moon: LRO cameras have mapped about 300 lunar pits, 16 of them in mare basalt; some open into voids that may be lava tubes (Wagner and Robinson).
lava_tubes.mars: Orbiter images show pit chains and skylight-like holes on the flanks of Mars's big shield volcanoes.

karst_caves.title: Caves for robots without GPS or light
karst_caves.why: Inside a cave a robot has no sun, no GPS and no radio link. It must navigate by what it senses itself.
karst_caves.gap: These caves are dissolved limestone and salt, not lava; useful for the robot, not the geology.

mare_basalt.title: Dark basalt plains like the lunar maria
mare_basalt.why: The lunar maria and most of Mars's crust are basalt. Excavators, sintered pads and oxygen extraction should be tested on it.
mare_basalt.gap: Earth basalt is weathered and often soil-covered; lunar mare basalt is bone-dry and fresh under regolith.
mare_basalt.moon: The dark lunar maria are basalt lava plains; Apollo 11, 12, 15 and 17 sampled them.
mare_basalt.mars: TES and other orbiter spectrometers show much of Mars's dark surface is basaltic.

highland_rock.title: Pale gabbro-family rock like the lunar highlands
highland_rock.why: The bright lunar highlands are anorthosite. The closest mapped class on Earth is gabbro and related deep-cooled rock.
highland_rock.gap: The global map lumps anorthosite with gabbro; true anorthosite massifs need a finer map.
highland_rock.moon: Apollo 16 returned highland anorthosite; 69 meteorites in NASA's catalogue are classed lunar anorthosite.

impact_rock.title: Impact-shocked rock
impact_rock.why: Craters are the main landform on the Moon and Mars. Shocked rock and impact melt are what samples will mostly be.
impact_rock.gap: Earth keeps only about 200 confirmed craters, most eroded or buried; the Moon and Mars keep millions.

volcanic_glass.title: Volcanic ash and glass beads
volcanic_glass.why: Apollo 17's orange soil was volcanic glass beads, a candidate feedstock for oxygen. Ash fields test handling and processing.
volcanic_glass.gap: Earth ash weathers to clay within thousands of years; lunar glass beads are billions of years old.

salt_biosig.title: Salt deposits that preserve traces of life
salt_biosig.why: Salt can trap and preserve organic molecules and microbes for very long times. It is a prime place to look for past life.
salt_biosig.gap: Earth salt flats hold living microbes today; Mars salt would hold only ancient traces, if any.
salt_biosig.mars: Mars Odyssey's THEMIS camera found about 640 chloride salt deposits across the ancient southern highlands (Osterloo et al. 2010).

oxidant_soil.title: Soil that destroys organic molecules
oxidant_soil.why: Mars soil chemistry and UV break down organics, so a life-detection instrument can miss what is there. Test it where the same happens.
oxidant_soil.gap: Earth's ozone blocks the harshest UV; oxidants form more slowly here.
oxidant_soil.mars: NASA's Phoenix lander found perchlorate, a strong oxidant, in Mars soil in 2008.

hydrothermal.title: Volcanic heat and water in dry land
hydrothermal.why: Hot springs build silica crusts that lock in traces of life. Spirit found silica-rich deposits on Mars that may have formed this way.
hydrothermal.gap: Earth springs are active and alive today; Mars deposits are billions of years old.

ancient_crust.title: Ancient exposed crust in dry land
ancient_crust.why: Most of the Moon's surface is over 3 billion years old. Earth's oldest exposed shields hold its earliest record.
ancient_crust.gap: Rock type is a proxy for age; the map does not date the rock.

seismic_quiet.title: Seismically quiet bedrock
seismic_quiet.why: Seismometers read a planet's interior. They are tested best on solid rock far from earthquakes and people.
seismic_quiet.gap: Earth's oceans and weather make background noise that the Moon does not have.
seismic_quiet.mars: NASA's InSight seismometer recorded 1,319 marsquakes before the mission ended in 2022.

magnetic_memory.title: Rock with strong fossil magnetism
magnetic_memory.why: Mars and the Moon lost their global magnetic fields, but some rocks kept the old magnetism. It is a record of an ancient planetary core.
magnetic_memory.gap: Earth still has an active field that dwarfs crustal anomalies; instruments must subtract it.
magnetic_memory.mars: Mars Global Surveyor mapped strong crustal magnetic fields, mostly in the ancient southern highlands.

radio_quiet.title: Far from people, signals and contamination
radio_quiet.why: Mars is minutes away by radio, so robots must decide alone; samples must stay free of Earth life. Test where people barely reach.
radio_quiet.gap: Distance to towns is a proxy; it does not measure radio noise directly.

dried_lakes.title: Dried ancient lake beds
dried_lakes.why: Mars had lakes and river deltas, such as Jezero crater where Perseverance landed. Dry lake beds on Earth keep the same kind of layered record.
dried_lakes.gap: Earth lake beds dried thousands of years ago; Mars's dried billions of years ago.

sand_ratio.title: Sand that moves like Mars sand (ratio match)
sand_ratio.why: On Mars, thin air means sand moves only in rare gusts. The match is not the windiest desert but sand seas where wind relative to the lift threshold is just as low.
sand_ratio.gap: Matches the wind-to-threshold ratio, not grain hop height; Mars grains fly higher and longer in low gravity.
sand_ratio.mars: Lifting a 0.25 mm grain takes about 1.1 m/s friction speed on Mars vs 0.24 on Earth. With typical Mars winds the ratio is about 0.36; Earth's median is 0.48.

ice_ratio.title: Ground ice balanced like Mars ice (ratio match)
ice_ratio.why: On Mars, ground ice lasts where the air's frost point equals the ground's mean temperature. The match is where the same balance holds, with almost no snow to resupply it.
ice_ratio.gap: Earth's balance also depends on summer melt and snow, which Mars lacks.
ice_ratio.mars: Mars mid-latitude ground ice sits near this balance line, which is why it is found shallow there (Phoenix dug into it at 68N).

erasers_off.title: Earth's erasers switched off
erasers_off.why: Water, life, earthquakes and people erase Earth's records. Where all four are weakest, Earth keeps records the way the Moon and Mars do.
erasers_off.gap: Wind and ice also erase; not yet included.
erasers_off.moon: Independent check with NASA's Meteorite Landings catalogue (31,085 finds on land, never given to the engine): 67% of finds lie in the top quarter of land where water, life and earthquakes are weakest (chance would give 25%). The median find sits at the 78th percentile.
erasers_off.mars: Independent check with NASA's Meteorite Landings catalogue (31,085 finds on land, never given to the engine): 67% of finds lie in the top quarter of land where water, life and earthquakes are weakest (chance would give 25%). The median find sits at the 78th percentile.

earth_cant.title: Vacuum
earth_cant.why: Changes heat flow, outgassing, lubrication and dust behaviour.

earth_cant.title: Low gravity (1/6 g Moon, 3/8 g Mars)
earth_cant.why: Changes walking, digging, traction and how dust falls.
earth_cant.instead: Parabolic flights, offloading rigs, neutral buoyancy

earth_cant.title: Space radiation
earth_cant.why: Damages electronics and crews over years.

earth_cant.title: Carbon dioxide geysers under seasonal ice
earth_cant.why: Spring gas jets near the Martian south pole.

earth_cant.title: Superconducting cold for free
earth_cant.why: Crater cold could run superconducting power lines and maglevs; nowhere on Earth is cold enough.

ground.note: thermal inertia, J m-2 K-1 s-1/2; under ~100 = loose dust, 150-400 = sand and crusted soil, over ~1000 = rock

water.note: Odyssey GRS water-equivalent wt%, top ~1 m, 5 deg bins
water.coverage: about 57S to 57N; ice-rich ground poleward is outside this map

base_zone.rule: GRS water over 5 wt%, below the areoid (thicker air), thermal inertia 150+ (firm), within 50 deg of equator

mobility.note: NASA's Scarecrow test rover was stripped so it weighs on Earth what Curiosity weighs on Mars: the ratio lens already used for wheels.
